To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
polycystin 1 dysfunction impairs urinary electrolyte handling and causes a renal tubular electrolyte defect in a renal precysitc mouse model for AD PKD.
PC1 is a key regulator of renal electrolyte handling, and that PC1 dysfunction results in a systemic electrolytic imbalance in a mouse model for AD PKD.
the loss of PC1 in the kidney results in electrolyte wasting, which is associated with downregulation of the key genes involved in electrolyte reabsorptive pathways.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the role of polycystin 1 in the renal electrolyte and water homeostasis.
a new aspect of PC1 function, namely its involvement in renal electrolyte and water homeostasis.
the elucidation of the molecular and physiological mechanisms underlying the renal electrolyte imbalance observed in ADPKD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PC1 dysfunction in a precystic ADPKD model impairs electrolyte handling in the kidney and leads to electrolyte disturbances in serum.
PC1 is required for renal electrolyte handling, and its dysfunction in ADPKD leads to electrolyte wasting and systemic electrolyte imbalance.
the loss of PC1 leads to electrolyte wasting and water reabsorption defects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PC1 dysfunction in the kidney causes a systemic electrolyte disturbance in a renal precyclic model for ADPKC.
PC1 is required for electrolyte re-absorption in TAL, DCT, and CNT, and for water reabsorption in collecting duct.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the renal handling of electrolytes is impaired in ADPKD even in the precystic stage of the disease, and that this may be a contributing factor to the development of cysts.

the loss of PC1 function in ADPKD leads to a renal electrolyte wasting phenotype that is present before cysts appear in the kidney and is therefore independent of the cyst formation process.
